0.0.n: A shortened まあ, used as a casual opening filler.

0.2.n: Casual 行っている, with い omitted; here it describes being at the place visited.

0.3.n: Follows a verb phrase to identify the time when something happens.

0.4.n: Marks とき as the time of the following thought.

0.7.n: A drawn-out reaction expressing pleasure or realization.

0.9.n: Casually intensifies 楽しい; more standard grammar would use すごく.

0.10.n: Describes the speaker's enjoyment inside the quoted thought.

0.12.n: Marks the preceding words as the content of the speaker's thought.

0.13.n: The て-form of 思う connects this thought to the continuing account.

1.0.n: Expresses surprise rather than asking for a straightforward answer.

1.1.n: Points to the surprising feeling the speaker is trying to describe.

1.3.n: Combines with まで to mean up to this point.

1.4.n: Sets 今 as the endpoint of the speaker's previous experience.

1.5.n: Past form of 味わう, used with こと to talk about having an experience.

1.6.n: Turns 味わった into an experience that can be described as never having happened.

1.7.n: Replaces が in this noun-describing phrase, marking こと as what has not existed.

1.8.n: Negates the existence of any prior experience, rather than directly negating 味わった.

1.9.n: 楽しい becomes a noun by replacing its final い with さ.

1.10.n: Lists 楽しさ alongside the other feelings that follow.

1.12.n: A casual filler showing the speaker is searching for the right description.

1.13.n: Names a feeling of release from restrictions or pressure.

1.14.n: Continues the list into the feeling described in the next line.

2.0.n: A hesitation filler here, not the word used before a noun to mean that.

2.2.n: A sharp reaction expressing surprise at the speaker's own realization.

2.4.n: Refers to the speaker; casual speech leaves out a following topic particle here.

2.6.n: Pairs with まで to refer to the period before this new experience.

2.7.n: Together with 今, establishes how things had been up to this point.

2.8.n: Links 今まで to 状態, describing the speaker's previous condition.

2.9.n: Refers to how the speaker's life or feelings were before this experience.

2.10.n: Marks the state that returning would lead back to.

2.11.n: 戻る takes the desire ending たい, which becomes たくない when negative.

2.12.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone to the speaker's reluctance.

2.13.n: Completes the casual explanatory expression んだ before けど.

2.14.n: Connects not wanting to return with uncertainty about what to do.

2.16.n: Combines with すればいい to ask what action would be best.

2.17.n: する becomes conditional すれば; adding いい asks which action would lead to a good result.

2.18.n: Ends a casual question seeking an explanation or solution.

2.21.n: Casual と言う introduces the quoted thought as a description of the feeling.

2.22.n: Names the emotional impression expressed by the preceding quoted thought.

2.23.n: Marks 感じ as what welled up in the next line.

3.0.n: An expressive word suggesting a light, soft emergence rather than a forceful surge.

3.1.n: A conversational word helping the speaker convey how the feeling appeared.

3.2.n: 湧く in て-form plus きた describes a feeling emerging into the speaker's awareness.

3.3.n: Casual と言う loosely sums up the experience while leaving the sentence open.

0.lit: Well, when I was there, I thought, Ah, so fun, and…
0.tip: と marks the quoted thought, while 思って links it to what follows.

1.lit: What, this… never-before-experienced joy, and, sort of, a sense of freedom, and…
1.tip: 味わったことのない describes 楽しさ as something the speaker had never experienced before.

2.lit: Um, a feeling like, Huh? I don't want to return to my previous state, but what should I do?
2.tip: どうすればいい asks what to do, literally asking how acting would be good.

3.lit: Gently, like this, welled up—that's how it was…
3.tip: The subject comes from the previous line: the feeling is what 湧いてきた describes as welling up.
